DANIEL OKAFOR-REYES
Backend Engineer | Java, Kotlin and Event-Driven Services

Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202
LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and operating production services in Java and Spring Boot, with additional Kotlin experience. Skilled in REST API design, PostgreSQL and relational database performance, Kafka-based event processing, automated testing, and cloud deployments on AWS EKS. Experienced with production on-call and reliability improvements. Has used Python for scripts and Jenkins helpers and is interested in moving into a Python-focused backend role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Backend: Java (8–17), Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Kotlin (basic), Python scripting
APIs and messaging: REST, OpenAPI 3, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Spring Cloud Contract
Databases and performance: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, JPA query tuning
Cloud and delivery: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Kubernetes, Docker, Helm, Jenkins, CI/CD
Testing and tools: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Git, Linux

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech, Lisbon
Jan 2022–Present
• Develop and maintain seven Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices supporting policy quoting and claims intake.
• Designed and versioned an OpenAPI 3 REST API for partner quoting; onboarded 12 broker partners handling approximately 400,000 quote requests per month.
• Added partner-specific rate limiting and contract tests using Spring Cloud Contract.
• Improved quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
• Resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox and idempotent consumers; duplicate records fell from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
• Deploy services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in a one-week-per-month on-call rota.
• Led the response to a significant Kafka lag incident in March 2024; the incident write-up was praised.
• Built a small internal Kotlin / Spring Boot service to render policy PDFs from templates using AWS S3 and SQS, and wrote the team's Kotlin coding guidelines.
• Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks (since 2024).
• Use Python for data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helper scripts; have not shipped a Python service.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A., Porto
Sep 2019–Dec 2021
• Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
• Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, increasing payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% and supporting safer refactoring.
• Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a Spring Boot service using RabbitMQ and Thymeleaf.

Junior Developer (Internship, then Full-Time) | CodeFarol Lda, Porto
Jul 2018–Aug 2019
• Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute, 2018

CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional: Java SE 11 Developer, 2020

LANGUAGES
English (fluent; professional working language at Tejo Insurance Tech)
Portuguese (fluent)
Spanish (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear backend engineering profile, relevant quantified achievements, and credible production experience. The progression from Java backend development to microservices, Kafka, Kubernetes, performance optimisation, incident response, and on-call ownership is compelling. The bullets are concise and outcome-oriented, especially the latency improvement, partner/API scale, and reduction of duplicate claims. The document is also appropriately transparent about Python experience, stating that Python has been used for scripts but not for production services. Minor completeness opportunities remain: the CV omits the Oracle Java certification and the backend guild leadership responsibility from the original candidate information, both of which could reinforce credibility and communication/ownership skills.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, conventional dates, searchable technology names, and a strong concentration of relevant keywords including Java, Kotlin, Python, Spring Boot, REST, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, EKS, automated testing, Jenkins, and CI/CD. The job title and summary are well aligned with a Python-transition backend role. AI screening probability is high because the document clearly connects technical skills to measurable production outcomes. The main minor limitation is that Docker, CI/CD, and some testing tools appear primarily in the skills section rather than being consistently tied to specific experience bullets. The CV also does not explicitly mention schema migrations, GitHub Actions, FastAPI, observability tooling, Terraform, logistics, or Dutch/French; these are candidate gaps or unsupported technologies and should not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a strong comparable-language match for the role. The CV shows seven years of professional backend experience in Java, additional Kotlin experience, willingness to move into a Python-focused role, REST API design, PostgreSQL and query tuning, Docker, AWS EKS deployment, automated testing, CI/CD, Kafka, Kubernetes, and production on-call work. The event-driven claims work and Kafka incident response align particularly well with the shipment event-ingestion and reliability focus. The quantified API and latency examples also support the public tracking API performance requirements. The CV demonstrates reliability ownership and incident response, which fit the company’s 'Be dependable' and ownership culture. PostgreSQL schema migrations are not shown in the candidate material, so that is a gap rather than a document defect. There is no logistics, transport, EDI, observability-tooling, Terraform, Dutch, or French experience in the supplied material. The candidate is based in Lisbon rather than Antwerp, but the ad allows candidates elsewhere in the EU to work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks; the CV does not need to state this unless relevant to the application.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the CERTIFICATION section, add the omitted certification from the original candidate information: "Oracle Certified Professional: Java SE 11 Developer, 2020." This adds a relevant, verifiable credential without changing the document’s positioning.
2. In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, add a concise ownership/communication bullet supported by the original information: "Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks since 2024, facilitating technical knowledge-sharing across the backend team." This strengthens alignment with the requirement to explain technical trade-offs clearly and with the company’s knowledge-sharing culture.
3. In the Professional Summary, revise the final sentence to make the comparable-language transition especially explicit: "Experienced primarily in Java/Spring Boot, with production Kotlin experience and Python scripting experience; interested in moving into a Python-focused backend role." This preserves the existing truthful disclosure while making the job’s Python-transition criterion easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.
4. In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, revise the deployment bullet to make the relevant delivery keywords more explicit without overstating ownership: "Deploy Java/Spring Boot services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Docker images, Helm charts, and Jenkins CI/CD pipelines; participate in a one-week-per-month on-call rota." Only retain "Docker images" if Docker was in fact used to build or package these deployed services, as supported by the candidate’s experience.

Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- Led the response to a significant Kafka lag incident in March 2024

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professionally structured CV with clear section headings, a logical reverse-chronological history, and highly credible quantified achievements. The strongest evidence includes the reduction in p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds, the reduction of duplicate claims to zero, the 400,000 monthly quote requests, and the improvement in test coverage from 35% to 70%. The document is also commendably transparent about Python being limited to scripting rather than claiming production Python service experience. Minor content limitations are that the summary repeats “experienced,” and the CV does not yet show the candidate’s Kafka-lag incident response and praised incident write-up, which would strengthen the production-reliability match.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard headings, plain text formatting, conventional dates, searchable technology names, and no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual symbols that would impede parsing. It contains strong matches for Java, Kotlin, Spring Boot, REST, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, automated testing, Jenkins, CI/CD, and on-call. AI screening probability is high for a comparable-language backend engineer role, but somewhat reduced for a strictly Python-first search because Python appears only as scripting and the CV does not mention FastAPI—which must not be added because it is not supported by the candidate information. The document appropriately avoids unsupported claims about Python services, Terraform, observability tools, logistics, or EDI.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the comparable-language pathway in the advertisement. It shows seven years of backend experience in Java, additional Kotlin production experience, PostgreSQL and query tuning, REST API design, Docker, AWS/EKS deployment, automated testing, CI/CD, Kafka, Kubernetes, and on-call operations. The production-quality and ownership themes also fit Tessel’s culture of dependable services and engineers who run what they build. The main genuine gaps are professional Python service development, schema migrations, Terraform implementation, observability tooling, logistics/transport/EDI experience, and Dutch or French. The candidate is based in Lisbon, which is compatible with the ad’s stated EU remote option, although the CV does not state the candidate’s hybrid preference. The document should continue to present Python as a transition target rather than imply existing Python service experience.
